name: LiTRA
description: LiTRA records the cost of running NIST Lightweight Cryptography AEAD algorithms as TLS 1.3 record-layer ciphers on embedded hardware. Five NIST LWC finalists are measured alongside the two standard TLS 1.3 baselines and an integrity-only control across twelve payload sizes, seven batch sizes, and five CPU clocks on a pair of ESP32-P4 boards communicating over Ethernet. Every row summarizes one batch of TLS records and carries 29 fields, spanning latency, throughput, cycle counts, per-byte cost, heap and stack consumption, and the static memory footprint of each cipher. The two boards are synchronized with IEEE 1588 Precision Time Protocol, so the client and server files are paired observations of the same traffic recorded from opposite ends of the link. The deposit holds five archives, one per CPU clock, each containing a client and a server CSV file. Field names, units, and provenance are documented in column_dictionary.csv. Measurement setup, experimental design, archive composition, and coverage notes are given in README.md, which should be read before use. Measurements were taken with ESP-IDF v5.5.2 and wolfSSL 5.7.2 extended with a cryptographic abstraction layer that exposes lightweight AEAD algorithms through the TLS 1.3 record layer.
